chapter: Woody Herman, Henderson and the Indiana Theater
title: Playing head arrangements for touring acts at the Indiana
summary: The theater band backed acts from the Oriental Theater and Chez Paree, reading music only sometimes and otherwise following a sung melody.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yes. So, I had that band there for quite a while there at the theater. And we played head arrangements.

We would get acts there, maybe say like an act would be booked down at the Oriental Theater, so you know it must have been a long time, because whenever the Oriental Theater been open, see, and we were getting acts from Sullivan's show, that would be booked down there. We would get acts from the Chez Paree, coming in here, --

-- and that would be a chance we'd get to read music. Other than that, they'd just come tell us, sing so-and-so. I mean, play so-and-so. Well, how does it go? And they'd start to sing it, and the piano would follow along and get it and we'd play it.
Yeah, I used to play shows like that.
Yes, shows, yeah. You've got to be a good musician to play a show like that.
Yeah, then we'd read some. They were almost like nightclub acts. Where was the Indiana?
43rd and Indiana. Just short blocks, just between Indiana and Calumet.
